.²1 Turning round, revolving, whirling.
.²2 Rolling onward, moving about; {#saMvartaprakawavivartasaptapATonATormivyatikaraviBramapracaRqaH#} <ls>Mv. 6. 26</ls>.
.²3 Rolling back, returning.
.²4 Dancing.
.²5 Alteration,

 modification, change of form, altered condition or state; {#SabdabrahmaRastAdfSaM#}
 {#vivartamitihAsaM rAmAyaRaM praRinAya#} <ls>U. 2</ls>; {#eko rasaH karuRa eva nimittaBedAdBinnaH#}
 {#pfTak pfTagivASrayate vivartAn#} <ls>U. 3. 47</ls>; {#akARqaSuzkASanipAtarOdraH#}
 {#ka eza DAturvizamo vivartaH#} <ls>Mv. 5. 57</ls>.
.²6 (In Vedānta <ab>phil.</ab>) An apparent or illusory form, an unreal appearance
 caused by {#avidyA#} or human error; (this is a favourite doctrine of
 the Vedāntins according to whom the whole visible world is a mere illusion
 --an unreal and illusory appearance-- while Brahman or Supreme Spirit
 is the only real entity; as a serpent ({#sarpa#}) is a {%vivarta%} of
 a rope ({#rajju#}), so is the world a {%vivarta%} of the real entity Brahman,
 and the illusion is removed by {%Vidyā%} or true knowledge; <ab>cf.</ab> Bhavabhūti:--
 {#vidyAkalpena marutA meGAnAM BUyasAmapi . brahmaRIva vivartAnAM kvApi#}
 {#vipralayaH kftaH ..#} <ls>U. 6. 6</ls>).
.²7 A heap, multitude, collection, an assemblage.

the doctrine of the Vedāntins that the visible world is
 illusory and Brahman alone is the real entity.
